Reds That Like It Cool: Two Côtes du Rhône Wines to Try Chilled

Nov 16, 2026Cindy RynningEurope, Events and Travel, Red Wine, Regional Wines, Wine Reviews, Wineries
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:30
Instaread

A few years ago, I solidified my appreciation for wines of the Rhône Valley when I hosted a group of winelovers on a river cruise along the Rhône River. From Avignon to Lyon, we swirled, sipped, and savored superior wines both on the ship as well as at tastings in Chateauneuf du Pape, Beaujolais, the Côtes du Rhône and more. There are so many memories from that trip and as I look at the myriad of photographs, I always come back to those with a glass of wine in someone’s hand! As luck would have it, just recently I was sent two wines (as samples) from the Côtes du Rhône for tasting and review. These well-priced wines are incredibly flavorful and food friendly (seriously, any menu item will work with a luscious glass of these red wine blends) and each can (and should) be considered a weekday wine for your daily dose of joie de vivre. Just remember to give each bottle a chill before opening. You won’t believe how even more enjoyable these wines will be!

 

The Côtes du Rhône AOC is in the Southern Rhône Valley

Vineyards in the Southern Rhône begin south of the town of Montelimar and are located in a wide swath on either side of the river until it passes south of Avignon. This large region produces about 95% of the total production with wines ranging from delicious, everyday choices to those considered ultra-premium. These wines are primarily red and are based on Grenache, Syrah, and Mourvèdre (GSM), also known as Rhône blends. Minor white varieties include Clairette, Grenache Blanc, and Bourboulenc.

Many vineyards are planted on a flat landscape with the best sites on stony soils that absorb the sun’s heat and warm the vineyard. The Mediterranean climate offers mild winters and hot dry summers; drought can be problematic. Heavy winds, known as the Mistral, may cause damage to the vines since there are fewer slopes to protect the vineyards.

Located in the Southern Rhône Valley is Côtes du Rhône. 86% of the production in both Côtes du Rhône and Côtes du Rhône Villages AOCs are red wine blends of the region’s key varieties: Grenache, Syrah, and Mourvedre. Are you ready to open that bottle? Winegrowers and negociants of the Côtes du Rhône AOCs suggest that reds should be chilled to bring out their fruit notes withouth altering the wine’s character. They are absolutely correct. Place wines in the refrigerator for about 20 minutes before serving to reach the ideal temperature of 59-61 degrees Fahrenheit. Now, pop the cork and enjoy each sip! Following are two exceptional wines to try.

Chateau Gigognan 2022 is Produced in AOC Côtes du Rhône Villages

From a well known vineyard in Chateauneuf-du-Pape, this lovely blend of Syrah, Grenache, and Mourvedre from Chateau Gigognan is produced at Bois des Moines in the AOC Côtes du Rhône Villages. Soils of marly sand and limestone terraces with a southern exposure on rolled pebbles are similar to those in Chateauneuf-du-Pape. 30 year old vines produced grapes that were harvested manually; the wine was aged for 18 months in tulip concrete vats and oak barrels. On the nose, I found aromas of cherries, pomegranate, hint of black pepper, and rich red berries. On the balanced, satin-like palate, notes of anise, dark plums, and raspberries were magnificent. This beauty can be aged for 5-10 years, so be sure to complement a juicy pork tenderloin, beef stew, eggplant parmigiana, or a raspberry tatin pie with chocolate praline ice cream for the win! Cost is around $31.

Tender pork for a brilliant pairing

Domaine Brusset 2025 from AOC Côtes du Rhône Pairs with Provencal Cuisine

Domaine Brusset is located in Cairanne, France, just north and slightly east of Avignon. The specific grape varieties of this blend are not confirmed, but my palate indicated that Grenache, Syrah, and Mourvedre are involved. Fresh and young, fruit showed plenty of energy. Terroir of clay-limestone soils and rolled pebbles helped suggest aromas of red and black fruit, and touches of spice and herbs. Its palate offered more red fruit, anise, spice, minerality, moderate tannic structure and acidity, and a medium finish. Enjoy a chilled glass or two with ratatouille, lamb with herbs of Provence, roast pork with fresh thyme, cheeses, and charcuterie. Of course, we can’t go wrong with a classic Provencal stew! Domaine Brusset 2025 can be enjoyed young, but cellared for a few years, it will shine even more. Cost is approximately $16.

Pour the slightly chilled wine from Cotes du Rhone and enjoy the lamb!

Cheers! ~ Cindy
